title.value: Conducting gender-based analysis of existing databases when self-reported gender data are unavailable: the GENDER Index in a working population
title.justification: The title clearly describes the focus of the research, which is about conducting gender-based analysis when self-reported gender data are unavailable, and it introduces the GENDER Index.
title.quote: Conducting gender-based analysis of existing databases when self-reported gender data are unavailable: the GENDER Index in a working population

analysis.description: The paper addresses the challenge of incorporating gender analysis in health research when self-reported gender data are missing. It introduces the GENDER Index, a composite gender score developed using data from the Canadian Community Health Survey (CCHS), to enable gender-based analysis in retrospective studies. The GENDER Index was derived from a logistic regression model using gender-related variables with biological sex as the dependent variable. The paper validates the GENDER Index's construct validity by demonstrating its relation to expected gender-related variables.

type.justification: The study includes a new composite index (GENDER Index), derived and validated using data from the Canadian Community Health Survey (CCHS). It involves empirical analysis, including statistical modeling and validation processes.
type.quote: This study aimed to create and validate a composite gender index using data from the Canadian Community Health Survey (CCHS).

name.justification: The research focuses on gender analysis in public health using existing health survey data.
name.quote: Objectives Growing attention has been given to considering sex and gender in health research... This study aimed to create and validate a composite gender index using data from the Canadian Community Health Survey (CCHS).

name.justification: The study involves analyzing existing health survey data to understand health trajectories and outcomes.
name.quote: The secondary analysis of such data sources is, nonetheless, indispensable to enriching our understanding of health trajectories, healthcare utilization, and real-world risks and benefits of drugs among large populations.

name.justification: The study involved the creation of a logistic regression model to develop the GENDER Index using gender-related variables as covariates.
name.quote: Among workers aged 18–50 years who had no missing data for our variables of interest (n = 29,470 participants), propensity scores were derived from a logistic regression model that included gender-related variables as covariates and where biological sex served as the dependent variable.
